terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where the demo compares a few pairs of values with your deepEqual.

tasks.title: Primitives, arrays and objects
tasks.description:
Implement `deepEqual(a, b)` in `src/deepEqual.js` for primitives, arrays and plain objects.

- Primitives are equal when `Object.is` says so: `NaN` equals `NaN`, but `0` and `-0` differ.
- Arrays are equal when they have the same length and deeply equal items in the same order.
- Plain objects are equal when they have the same own keys, in any order, with deeply equal values. `{ a: undefined }` is not equal to `{}`.
- Values of different kinds are never equal: an array is not a plain object, and `null` is not `{}`.

The check compares hidden pairs both ways round, so `deepEqual(a, b)` and `deepEqual(b, a)` must agree.
nextSteps: Handle the case where both values are the same primitive or the same object.
Return false early when either side is not an object.
Compare arrays, then plain objects, by calling deepEqual on their parts.
Run `node src/demo.js` and read the first two lines.
hints: `typeof null` is `'object'`, and arrays are objects too. Decide the kind of each side before you compare contents.
`Object.is` handles `NaN` and `-0` the way this task wants. For objects, compare key counts first, then check that every key of `a` exists on `b`.
Comparing prototypes with `Object.getPrototypeOf` is a simple way to make sure both sides are the same kind before you look inside.

tasks.title: Dates, maps and sets
tasks.description:
Extend `deepEqual` to built-in types.

- Two `Date` values are equal when they hold the same time. Two invalid dates are equal.
- Two `Map` values are equal when they have the same keys (found with `has`) and deeply equal values for each key.
- Two `Set` values are equal when they have the same members (found with `has`), in any order.
- A `Date`, `Map` or `Set` is never equal to a value of another kind, such as a plain object or an array.

The check covers equal and unequal pairs of each kind, empty ones, mixed kinds and built-ins nested inside objects.
nextSteps: Find out why a Date and an empty object look equal to your task 1 code.
Add a branch for each built-in before the plain object branch.
Compare map values with deepEqual itself.
Run the demo and read the third line.
hints: Dates, maps and sets keep their contents outside their own keys, so `Object.keys` sees nothing.
`instanceof` tells you which built-in you have. Make sure both sides are the same kind first.
For maps: compare sizes, then for each `[key, value]` of one map check `has(key)` on the other and compare `value` deeply. Sets work the same way without values.

tasks.title: Cyclic references
tasks.description:
Make `deepEqual` work when values refer to themselves.

- An object, array or map may contain itself, directly or through a chain of other values. `deepEqual` must return an answer instead of overflowing the stack.
- Differences inside cyclic structures must still be found.
- The same object can appear in several places without forming a cycle. Every place is still compared with its own counterpart.

The check also compares two structures of 100,000 objects that all point back to their root, and expects the answer in well under 2 seconds.
nextSteps: Decide what to remember so that meeting it again stops the recursion.
Pass that memory down through every recursive call.
Try the shared object case from the task description by hand.
Make the lookup constant time, then rerun the check.
hints: If you are already in the middle of comparing two values and meet the same two again, you can treat them as equal for now. Any real difference will be found on the first visit.
Remembering only the left value is wrong: the same left object can meet a different right object somewhere else.
Keep a `Map` from each left object to a `Set` of right objects already paired with it. Check and record the pair before you look inside.
